channel.title: International Consortium of Investigative Journalists ICIJ - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from International Consortium of Investigative Journalists ICIJ (icij.org)

item.title: Former Nigerian oil minister stands trial in the UK on bribery charges
item.description: Prosecutors accused former minister Diezani Alison-Madueke, who featured in the ICIJ-led Panama Papers investigation, of living a “life of luxury in London” fueled by corrupt Nigerian oil deals.

item.title: Mexican cartels overpower police with ammunition made for the US military
item.description: Drug syndicates have used .50-caliber ammunition produced at a plant owned by the U.S. Army and smuggled across the border in attacks on Mexican civilians and police.

item.title: Nearly half of powerful .50-caliber ammo seized by Mexican government came from US Army plant, defense minister says
item.description: Mexican officials shared the data in response to an investigation by ICIJ and media partners.

item.title: As crypto industry expands, U.S. slashes office examining dirty money safeguards of cryptocurrency exchanges
item.description: The number of IRS staff assigned to oversee anti-money laundering practices at the firms dropped to its lowest level in nearly decade.

item.title: Hong Kong firms feed European tech to Russia’s war in Ukraine, report says
item.description: Researchers at the Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong Foundation identify Hong Kong as a key hub in the illicit trade of Western military technology to Russia.

item.title: Massachusetts sues Bitcoin Depot, alleging the crypto ATM operator knowingly facilitated crypto scams
item.description: The Massachusetts Attorney General’s lawsuit is the latest in a series of state legal actions against one of the world’s largest crypto ATM operators.

item.title: Greek court convicts Intellexa founder Tal Dilian, three others in wiretapping scandal
item.description: The former Israeli intelligence officer’s spyware has helped some of the world’s most brutal regimes spy on journalists and political opponents.

item.title: Advocacy group files formal grievance claiming World Bank ‘failed’ to address harm caused by controversial Tanzanian project
item.description: The project, which aimed to expand protected environmental areas and boost tourism, was terminated in 2024 after allegations of human rights abuses.

item.title: IRS criminal referrals against big corporations and ultrawealthy plummeted during Trump’s first year
item.description: New data shows how a key office hammered by layoffs and cost-cutting referred at most two cases in fiscal year 2025.

item.title: Lawmakers seek to stop sales to the public of ammunition made at U.S. Army plant
item.description: A new bill backed by Sen. Elizabeth Warren and three other Democrats came in response to an ICIJ and The New York Times investigation.
